_readme: Single source of truth for store listing text. scripts/store-check.mjs validates the lengths against the cited limits. Paste these values into each store dashboard (see chrome.md, firefox.md, edge.md for field mapping).

name.limit_source: Chrome Web Store dashboard item-name field is capped at 45 characters; this value is 16 and is safe under every store's cap. The name lives in src/manifest.json 'name', which all three stores display as the listing name. Operator picked 'Leia Reads' on 2026-10-14, then reverted to 'Leia: Read Aloud' the same day after the first AMO submission (guid leia@rclb.dev preserved; only the listing name changed).

short_description.value: Read any webpage aloud with a voice you choose and a highlight that follows the words as they are spoken.
short_description.limit_source: Manifest description limit of 132 characters: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/preparing/ (quoted: 'A string of no more than 132 characters'). Displayed by CWS as the short description; AMO and Edge use it the same way from the manifest.

amo_summary.value: Leia reads webpages aloud with a highlight that follows the words. Browser voices, a built-in offline model, local servers, or your own provider key. No account.
amo_summary.limit_source: AMO summary limit of 250 characters: https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/develop/create-an-appealing-listing/ (quoted: 'The summary description for your add-on is limited to 250 characters').

long_description_limit_note: The CWS dashboard enforces a 16,000-character detailed-description cap; the current text is ~2k so the exact cap is not load-bearing. Not encoded as a hard gate.

keywords_tags.usage: AMO tags (Basic Information) and Edge search terms. CWS has no keyword field; keywords belong naturally in the description. 'screen reader' was deliberately excluded: Leia is follow-along TTS, not a screen reader, and stores police misleading metadata.

categories.note: AMO allows up to two categories (source: create-an-appealing-listing). Verify the exact category strings in each dashboard at submission time; these are the intended picks.

_url_note: No public homepage, support page, or hosted privacy policy exists yet (checked PRODUCT.md and the repo). Fill these before submission if you can; every store field that takes them is optional except where the README notes otherwise. store/privacy-policy.md is written to be hosted anywhere (GitHub Pages or the repo itself) and its URL pasted into the dashboards.
